title: An incubation water eDNA method for a non-destructive rapid molecular identification of Pinna nobilis and Pinna rudis bivalve juveniles
author: Catanese, Tena-Medialdea, et al.

steps.title: House each juvenile in aquarium
steps.instruction: Place each of the 40 captured Pinna juveniles in an individual 200 mL aquarium and keep them for 24 h.

steps.title: Collect and filter water sample
steps.instruction: After 24 h, remove the juvenile, empty the aquarium, and filter the 200 mL water through a sterile cellulose membrane (0.45 µm pore size).

steps.title: Store filter for DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Allow the filter to dry, place it in an Eppendorf tube and store at –80 °C. Keep one half of the filter for extraction and retain the other half as backup.

steps.title: Extract DNA from filter
steps.instruction: Using a DNeasy PowerWater kit (Qiagen) and following the manufacturer’s protocol, extract total DNA from the half‑filter retained for analysis.

steps.title: Assess DNA quality and quantity
steps.instruction: Measure the extracted DNA with a Nanodrop 2000 spectrophotometer (ThermoScientific) and record concentration and purity before proceeding to PCR.

steps.title: Prepare control DNA from mantle tissue
steps.instruction: Collect mantle tissue from dead adult P. nobilis and P. rudis individuals, extract DNA with the NucleoSpin® Tissue DNA Isolation Kit (Macherey‑Nagel) according to the kit instructions.

steps.title: Set up multiplex PCR
steps.instruction: Prepare a multiplex PCR mix containing the extracted sample DNA, primers targeting the mitochondrial rRNA16S and rRNA12S genes (species‑specific 3′‑OH ends), and primers for the 28S rRNA fragment. Adjust primer amounts, annealing temperature and reagent concentrations as previously optimized for high‑efficiency, species‑specific amplification.

steps.title: Run PCR with optimized conditions
steps.instruction: Perform the PCR using the optimized cycling parameters (temperature profile and concentrations established during method development).

steps.title: Visualize PCR products on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Run the PCR products on an agarose gel alongside a 50 bp DNA ladder. Identify the universal 205 bp band (28S rRNA) and the species‑specific bands: 175 bp (12S, P. nobilis) or 123 bp (16S, P. rudis).

steps.title: Validate specificity on other bivalves
steps.instruction: Apply the same PCR conditions to DNA from mantle tissue of other bivalves (A. pectinata, M. edulis, M. galloprovincialis, O. edulis; total of 8 samples) and confirm that no cross‑amplification of the diagnostic fragments occurs.

steps.title: Confirm positive identifications by sequencing
steps.instruction: Purify any diagnostic amplicon that yields a positive result and sequence it using verification primers to confirm species identity.
